actions.desc: Channel measured in mode 2 (single-channel). LOGICAL channel: 0=V1, 1=V2, 2=V3, 3=I. Not an ADS1120 AIN number - the board wires the voltage senses in the opposite order (V1 on AIN2, V3 on AIN0), which the firmware hides behind VCP_CHANNEL_AIN_MAP.

Output sample rate per channel (SPS). The ADC always runs flat out; this sets how many conversions are averaged into each output sample, so a lower rate is quieter, not coarser. Named _conf.rate so the master moves its poll interval with it - a device rate change alone would silently drop frames, since one poll carries at most 16 frames in mode 1 (4-channel, 8-byte frames) or 64 samples in mode 2 (single channel, 2-byte samples). Rates must divide 1000 exactly and not exceed 1000 - the device rejects anything else rather than rounding, so e.g. 400 is not available. 125/200/250 work in either mode; 500 and 1000 are above the ~440 SPS/ch mode-1 ADC ceiling and are mode 2 only. Each map entry picks the poll interval giving ~28% catch-up headroom over the production rate, with s holding ~1s of history.
Per-channel linear calibration from an Excel fit (reading = k*true + c)
